 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Sacramento Kings committed $140 million to Keegan Murray over the next five seasons, and he has not bounced back from a regression in his fifth season.
 Murray is averaging 9.9 points on 39.1% from the field and 22.2% from three, both career lows in seven games. He's earning $24 million in the first year of his new deal and will end at $31.8 million in 2030-31.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Even his nagging left ankle injuries have limited him this season . The 26-year-old missed seven games with left ankle capsulitis.
 His average annual earnings are about the going rate for a quality starter across the league. Sacramento hasn't gotten that kind of production from him, sparking intense fan scrutiny.
 The Kings' 2022 first-round pick has been slowly regressing ever since a breakout rookie season. Murray broke Donovan Mitchell's single-season record for 3-pointers made by a rookie, playing a vital role in helping the franchise break a 16-year playoff drought.
 He was brimming with potential as a two-way forward who can space the floor, rebound and defend. Sacramento nailed its No. 4 pick, drafting a talented, young player who would be part of the team's future.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Its stance on Murray likely hasn't changed. Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. needs 3-and-D wings, like his fifth-year teammate, to mask his defensive deficiencies and capitalize on the open looks he generates.
 However, if the descent from rookie phenom to struggling shooter continues, the Kings may have to sell high.
 General manager Scott Perry is not shy about parting with young prospects in his first several seasons. Perry salary dumped Devin Carter and a second-round pick to the Atlanta Hawks , and he did the same with Nique Clifford, sending him to the Oklahoma City Thunder for two second-round picks.
 A change of scenery can become necessary for struggling or disgruntled players. His skill set alone is likely worth a gamble for trade suitors, especially contending teams.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Murray is trying to find his footing amid a seven-game losing streak. He's encouraging his teammates and keeping their spirits up, telling them if they can string together wins, they can turn Golden 1 Center into true home-court advantage .
 There are many worse contracts across the league, and Murray is far from that range. His struggles are discouraging for Kings fans and media who saw what he could be.
 The expectations surrounding him to improve are gone. Five years into a career, fans and media have accepted that Murray isn't likely going to ascend into an All-Star-caliber talent.
